en.question: Who were the United Empire Loyalists?
options: Over 40,000 people loyal to the British Crown who fled the American Revolution to settle in Nova Scotia and Quebec
French settlers who supported the British after the Plains of Abraham
Soldiers who fought in the War of 1812
Aboriginal nations who allied with the French
en.explanation: Page 26: 'More than 40,000 people loyal to the Crown, called "Loyalists," fled the oppression of the American Revolution to settle in Nova Scotia and Quebec.' They were a diverse group including Aboriginal Mohawk led by Joseph Brant and about 3,000 black Loyalists.

Loyalists were primarily of British, German, Dutch and Aboriginal origins fleeing the AMERICAN Revolution — not French settlers in Quebec.
The War of 1812 was a separate conflict 30+ years later. The defenders included British soldiers, Canadian volunteers and First Nations — not specifically called Loyalists.
Those were the Algonquin, Montagnais and Huron alliances under Champlain (p. 25) — completely unrelated to the Loyalists, who came over 150 years later.

Because France was banned from trading
Because Canada had fewer natural resources

en.question: Why does the Duke of Wellington feature in Canadian history?
options: He chose Bytown (Ottawa) as the endpoint of the Rideau Canal, helping found the national capital
He served as Canada's first Prime Minister
He led the Charge of the Light Brigade
He founded the Hudson's Bay Company
en.explanation: Page 30: 'The Duke of Wellington sent some of his best soldiers to defend Canada in 1814. He then chose Bytown (Ottawa) as the endpoint of the Rideau Canal, part of a network of forts to prevent the U.S.A. from invading Canada again.
